nodes.label: R-GEO-1
nodes.statement: NIR transmission (or transflection) is the preferred geometry for transparent or semi-transparent liquids (source example - dairy streams such as skim milk, whey, permeate).

nodes.label: R-GEO-2
nodes.statement: Transmission fails when the sample is too thick, opaque or fat-rich because light cannot penetrate it.

nodes.label: R-GEO-3
nodes.statement: NIR diffuse reflection suits opaque, concentrated or scattering samples (Table 1 also lists it for powders).

nodes.label: R-GEO-4
nodes.statement: Reflection can be less representative for clear liquids.

nodes.label: R-GEO-5
nodes.statement: In the dairy example, a transflection probe can "in some cases" serve both low-fat and high-fat products; for other low/high-scattering streams this is a hypothesis to test.

nodes.label: R-GEO-6
nodes.statement: Reflection signals are sensitive to surface characteristics and particle/globule size, so physical variation can mimic composition change; scatter correction is needed.

nodes.label: R-GEO-7
nodes.statement: In UV-Vis, a transmission signal saturates in high optical density media; a UV-ATR probe with its very short path can measure black or highly scattering fluids.

nodes.label: R-MIR-1
nodes.statement: MIR absorption is strong, so MIR needs very thin samples or ATR; ATR is the usual in-line route, and MIR transflexion fiber probes also exist.

nodes.label: R-MIR-2
nodes.statement: ATR requires tight contact; it suits liquids, pastes and soft solids.

nodes.label: R-MIR-3
nodes.statement: ATR samples only a surface layer a few micrometres deep, so deposits on the crystal and surface representativeness are risks.

nodes.label: R-MIR-4
nodes.statement: The MIR range is 4000-400 cm-1 (2.5-25 µm); MIR spectra have well-defined bands and high selectivity.

nodes.label: R-NIR-1
nodes.statement: NIR penetrates up to several millimetres, works with glass optics and standard lamps, and suits remote fiber-probe measurement.

nodes.label: R-NIR-2
nodes.statement: NIR bands are broad and overlapping; quantitative use needs a chemometric calibration.

nodes.label: R-NIR-3
nodes.statement: The nominal NIR range is 780-2500 nm; the usable range depends on the instrument, fiber and probe actually used.

nodes.label: R-NIR-4
nodes.statement: NIR may lack sensitivity for trace components (the source cites below 0.1 percent in a bioprocess context).

nodes.label: R-RAM-1
nodes.statement: Raman signals are weak and can be swamped by fluorescence; filters and special probe designs help, and fluorescence background must be checked on real samples.

nodes.label: R-RAM-2
nodes.statement: Raman is well suited to aqueous media because water interferes less than in infrared methods.

nodes.label: R-RAM-3
nodes.statement: Report Raman as Raman shift (cm-1) and state the laser excitation wavelength separately.

nodes.label: R-FLU-1
nodes.statement: Fluorescence only measures species that fluoresce (or a justified fluorescent indicator); most chemicals do not.

nodes.label: R-FLU-2
nodes.statement: Fluorescence has high sensitivity but low selectivity; it is not a direct measurement of every analyte.

nodes.label: R-FLU-3
nodes.statement: In bioprocesses, fluorescence is used for intrinsic fluorophores such as NADH, tryptophan and riboflavin.

nodes.label: R-UV-1
nodes.statement: UV-Vis is very sensitive but signals of mixtures overlap strongly, so chemometrics are needed and selectivity is low.

nodes.label: R-UV-2
nodes.statement: Turbidity (optical density) tracks cell density as a biomass proxy, but optical density is not a viable cell count.

nodes.label: R-FIB-1
nodes.statement: A fiber must transmit the method's spectral range. Silica fibers end near 2.4 µm, so they cannot carry MIR light; MIR needs chalcogenide (CIR), polycrystalline (PIR) fibers or hollow waveguides.

nodes.label: R-FIB-2
nodes.statement: Long (100-300 m) cables are stated only for low-OH silica fibers. The MIR fiber and hollow-waveguide samples compared on S02 p.9-10 are 1-2 m laboratory lengths. No source states an achievable length for an MIR link, so any MIR link length is an open question for AFS, not a value to assume.

nodes.label: R-FIB-3
nodes.statement: Hollow waveguides couple poorly to FTIR spectrometers; PIR fibers couple much better.

nodes.label: R-FIB-4
nodes.statement: Metal-coated silica fibers avoid polymer-jacket fluorescence, which matters for Raman and fluorescence.

nodes.label: R-FIB-5
nodes.statement: Fiber optics let sensitive spectrometers sit away from vibration and dust at the process point.

nodes.label: R-CAL-1
nodes.statement: NIR and Raman calibrations are specific to the matrix; after a change of sample matrix or composition the calibration must be re-validated (and usually rebuilt or extended) on the new material.

nodes.label: R-CMB-1
nodes.statement: Combining methods can help for complex samples, but a gain is a hypothesis; compare with the best single method and align sampling location and timing.

nodes.label: R-CMB-2
nodes.statement: For heterogeneous samples, different methods must sample the same small area; alternating separate probes cannot guarantee this, combined probes can.

nodes.label: R-CMB-3
nodes.statement: Data from several methods must be synchronised to a common time step before fusion.

nodes.label: R-EVI-1
nodes.statement: A laboratory or research study cannot be cited as proof of process or clinical readiness.

nodes.label: R-EVI-2
nodes.statement: A published application is a reason to test a method, not proof that it will work for a new customer.

nodes.label: R-EVI-3
nodes.statement: Spectra of frozen/thawed (ex vivo) samples can differ from in vivo measurements. The source notes model transfer was shown in other work (Raman), but there is no in vivo evidence for the sensor studied; ex vivo results do not establish in vivo use.

nodes.label: R-EVI-4
nodes.statement: The bioprocess variable map (Fig. 7) lists literature-reported accessible variables, not demonstrated AFS capability.

nodes.label: R-GEN-1
nodes.statement: A nominal method range is not the range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe; state only the usable range of the selected configuration.

nodes.label: R-GEN-2
nodes.statement: A feasibility plan needs representative samples or process states, independent reference measurements, a defined comparison and a go/no-go basis.

nodes.label: R-GEN-3
nodes.statement: Water absorbs much more strongly in infrared methods than in Raman. In aqueous samples MIR needs a very thin layer or ATR; NIR transmission needs a limited, controlled pathlength (see R-GEN-4); Raman tolerates water.

nodes.label: R-GEN-4
nodes.statement: In NIR transmission the optical pathlength must be controlled (usually 1-10 mm in the dairy example); too wide loses signal to absorption, too narrow samples a negligible volume.

nodes.label: R-GEN-5
nodes.statement: Sample inhomogeneity and process turbulence must be considered when choosing the measurement technique and sampling location.

nodes.label: R-PRO-1
nodes.statement: When the sample composition or target is not well known, start with multi-method laboratory trials on representative samples to select the method.

nodes.label: R-PRO-2
nodes.statement: An "insufficient information" status is a valid outcome; ask the deciding questions and propose the next step instead of guessing.

nodes.label: R-PRO-3
nodes.statement: Never invent spectra, results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths or other performance figures, client facts, product codes or prices.
